How a Game of League Works

The goal of the game, the five roles, and how a match flows from the first minion wave to the final push.

The goal: destroy the Nexus

League of Legends is a 5 versus 5 game. Each team has a base with a big crystal called the Nexus. Destroy the enemy Nexus and you win. That's it. Kills, gold and dragons only matter because they help you get to the enemy Nexus.

The Nexus is protected by towers (also called turrets) and inhibitors. You can't hit the Nexus until you've broken through at least one lane's towers and its inhibitor, plus the two towers right in front of the Nexus.

Common mistakeChasing kills all game and forgetting towers. A team with fewer kills but more towers often wins. When the enemy is dead or far away, hit a tower.

Three lanes and a jungle

The map, called Summoner's Rift, has three paths between the bases: top lane, middle lane and bottom lane ("bot"). Every 30 seconds, each Nexus sends out a wave of small computer-controlled soldiers called minions down every lane. The first wave arrives at 0:30.

Between the lanes is the jungle, full of neutral monsters that give gold and experience. A river cuts through the middle of the map. Learn the details in Summoner's Rift: The Map Explained.

The five roles

Each player has a job, decided in champion select:

  • Top: plays alone in top lane, usually a tough fighter or tank. See Top Lane.
  • Jungle: farms the monsters in the jungle and surprises enemy lanes (a "gank"). See Jungle.
  • Mid: plays alone in the middle lane, often a mage or assassin with big damage. See Mid Lane.
  • Bot (also called ADC, attack damage carry): a ranged marksman who deals steady damage from a distance. See Bot Lane (ADC).
  • Support: plays bot lane with the ADC, protects the team and places vision. See Support.

Each role also gets a role quest automatically: a goal that gives a reward when you complete it by playing your lane. More on that in Teamwork, Pings and Role Quests.

Gold, experience and items

Everyone starts with 500 gold at level 1. You earn gold by landing the final hit on minions and monsters (called a last hit), by killing champions, and by breaking towers. You spend gold in your base's shop on items that make you stronger.

You earn experience (XP) just by being near enemy minions when they die. XP raises your level, up to 18. Each level gives you more stats and a point to put into one of your four abilities. Your ultimate ability (R) unlocks at level 6.

Pro tipThe champion with more gold and levels usually wins a fight. That's why farming minions is the first skill to learn.

Start with Last-Hitting 101.

How a game flows

Games usually last 25 to 35 minutes and go through three phases:

  • Early game (laning phase, about 0-14 min): everyone stays in their lane, farms minions and tries to win small fights against their opponent. Junglers move around and help lanes.
  • Mid game (about 14-25 min): outer towers start falling. Teams move around the map to take objectives like dragons, the Rift Herald and towers.
  • Late game (25+ min): champions have most of their items. Big 5 versus 5 teamfights around Baron Nashor and the Elder Dragon decide the game. One lost fight can mean a lost Nexus.

What to focus on in your first games

League has a lot to learn, so don't try to learn it all at once. For your first games, pick one or two easy champions and focus on just these things:

  1. Last-hit as many minions as you can.
  2. Glance at the minimap (bottom-right corner) every few seconds.
  3. Go back to base when you're low on health instead of staying and dying.
  4. Join your team when they fight over dragons or towers.

Play the tutorial and some games against bots first. They're a safe place to learn your champion's abilities.

Key takeaways

  • You win by destroying the enemy Nexus, not by getting the most kills.
  • There are three lanes plus the jungle, and five roles: top, jungle, mid, bot and support.
  • Gold comes mainly from last-hitting minions; XP comes from being near minions when they die.
  • Games move from laning, to fighting over objectives, to big late-game teamfights.
  • In your first games, focus on farming, the minimap, and not dying.
